title: Author of Good, We Rest on Thee
description: Author of Good, We Rest on Thee in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: James Merrick wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 260, “"He Knoweth What Ye Have Need Of."”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Au-thor of good, we rest on Thee; Thine ev-er watch-ful eye A-lone our re-al wants can see, Thy hand a-lone sup-ply.

lines: Author of good, we rest on Thee;
Alone our real wants can see,
O, let Thy power be our defence,
And since, by passion's force subdued,
We blindly shun the latent good,
Not what we wish, but what we want,
The good unasked, O Father, grant;

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: James Merrick died in 1769.
credits: Words by James Merrick (1720–1769), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
